study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Elad et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si4_title: Improving the predictive potential of diffusion MRI in schizophrenia using normative models -Towards subject-level classification

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study aim and why normative modeling is applied: to test whether normative modeling improves subject-level predictions in schizophrenia using dMRI, and to evaluate classification performance. This satisfies both criteria (stated objectives and purpose of applying normative modeling).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "...to study whether normative modeling can improve subject-level predictions from a binary classifier... individual deviations from a normative model... were calculated..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They build a new normative model from healthy controls. The paper reports final sample sizes and cites the original publication for demographics, inclusion/exclusion criteria, acquisition protocols, preprocessing, and harmonization, but does not list detailed eligibility criteria, image quality standards, or exclusion reasons within this article.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The dataset used in this study coincides with the dataset... 601 individuals ... and 512 healthy controls... dMRI data were collated from 13 different sites... The single shell dMRI data followed a standardized preprocessing protocol and were harmonized... A complete account of demographics, inclusion and exclusion criteria, acquisition protocols across the 13 sites, preprocessing and harmonization procedures can be found in Cetin-Karayumak et al. (2020)."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled in the normative model via a nonparametric Nadaraya–Watson estimator with Gaussian kernel, computed separately by sex and centered on age. Multi-site effects are addressed via retrospective harmonization across 13 sites.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "To control for confounding factors resulting from age and sex differences, we represented the normative range... for each sex separately. To do so, we used the Nadaraya–Watson (NW) estimator... with a Gaussian kernel." | "...dMRI data were collated from 13 different sites... standardized preprocessing protocol and were harmonized across sites to remove site-related differences using retrospective harmonization..."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source is described as a large harmonized multi-site dMRI dataset (13 sites) with explicit citation to the source study (Cetin-Karayumak et al., 2020).
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The dataset used in this study coincides with the dataset utilized in the published work by (Cetin-Karayumak et al., 2020)... dMRI data were collated from 13 different sites..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from existing multi-site datasets are used; per guidance, image acquisition protocol is not applicable here (details are in the cited source study).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They state use of a standardized preprocessing protocol and retrospective harmonization across sites, citing relevant methods papers, and describe post-harmonization resolution and b-value. However, specific preprocessing software and QC procedures are not detailed in this article.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The single shell dMRI data followed a standardized preprocessing protocol and were harmonized across sites to remove site-related differences using retrospective harmonization (Karayumak et al., 2019; Ning et al., 2020)... Following harmonization, all data had isotropic resolution of 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm, with a b-value of 1,000 s/mm²."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They use a 10-fold cross-validation scheme with explicit partition sizes. Importantly, in each cross-validation, the normative range and bandwidth are estimated using only training-set healthy controls, ensuring test data are not used for fitting.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Prediction performance... validated using a 10-fold cross-validation... In each cross-validation... the normative range, as well as the choice of a bandwidth, were estimated using only the healthy control subjects that belonged to the corresponding training set."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset is used to validate the normative model; all validation is internal via 10-fold cross-validation on the assembled dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Prediction performance... validated using a 10-fold cross-validation..." (no external dataset mentioned).

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: a nonparametric Nadaraya–Watson estimator with Gaussian kernel to model age- and sex-adjusted normative ranges; bandwidth chosen by cross-validation with leave-one-out; z-scores computed per ROI; classification via logistic regression with ridge regularization; toolbox cited.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "...we used the Nadaraya–Watson (NW) estimator... with a Gaussian kernel... To set h for every ROI... we minimized the cross-validation function... the leave-one-out-estimator..." | "We chose logistic regression with ridge regularization (McIlhagga, 2016)..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: No quantitative fit or calibration metrics of the normative model (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage) are reported. Reported metrics focus on downstream classification AUC rather than normative model performance itself.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The average of the area under the receiver operator curve (AUC)... was the evaluation metric." (no normative model fit metrics reported).

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Sample sizes for each of the 10 cross-validation partitions are reported, but demographic characteristics per partition (e.g., age, sex) are not provided.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "...ten subsets — seven subsets comprised of 51 controls and 60 schizophrenia, two subsets comprised of 52 controls and 60 schizophrenia, and one subset comprised of 51 controls and 61 schizophrenia."

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Some implementation details and tools are cited (e.g., ridge logistic regression via a MATLAB toolbox; standardized preprocessing and harmonization references). However, software/library versions are not specified, and code, trained models, or data access conditions are not described in this article.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "We chose logistic regression with ridge regularization (McIlhagga, 2016)..." | "...standardized preprocessing protocol and were harmonized across sites... (Karayumak et al., 2019; Ning et al., 2020)."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Secondary data are used; the article cites the source for inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes that standardized preprocessing and harmonization were applied. Final sample sizes are reported, but detailed eligibility criteria, image quality standards, and exclusion reasons are not provided here.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "...601 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia-spectrum disorder... and 512 healthy controls... dMRI data were collated from 13 different sites... standardized preprocessing... harmonized... A complete account of demographics, inclusion and exclusion criteria... can be found in Cetin-Karayumak et al. (2020)."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses focus on imaging-derived features and demographic covariates (age, sex). The paper explicitly notes that heterogeneity in treatment protocols and comorbid substance use were not accounted for, and relationships to clinical symptoms were beyond scope.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "...the analysis we performed did not account for the data heterogeneity in the context of different treatment protocols and different comorbid substance use/abuse... Lastly, investigating the relationship between clinical symptoms and the brain abnormalities found is beyond the scope of the current article..."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort data sources are specified as multi-site dMRI collections (13 sites) with citation to the source publication.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "...dMRI data were collated from 13 different sites across a number of separate studies... A complete account... can be found in Cetin-Karayumak et al. (2020)."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes and demographics (mean age, SD, sex distribution) are reported for schizophrenia and control groups; clinical characteristics (e.g., medication status, symptom severity, illness duration) are not described.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "...601 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia-spectrum disorder (mean [SD] age, 31.46 [12.31] years; 380 [63.23%] male), and 512 healthy controls (mean [SD] age, 30.15 [14.26] years; 279 [54.49%] male)."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical assessment measures (e.g., rating scales, diagnostic instruments) and procedures are not described in this article; the focus is on imaging features and classification.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "...investigating the relationship between clinical symptoms and the brain abnormalities found is beyond the scope of the current article..."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define the meaning and thresholds of deviation scores (supra-normal vs infra-normal; |z| > 2.999) and specify directional hypotheses for modalities (lower FA/FAt, higher FW in schizophrenia). They discuss implications for classification but provide limited clinical significance beyond imaging-based interpretation.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "To define abnormal z-scores we used the threshold of |z| > 2.999... ROIs with z-scores above 2.999 were defined as supra-normal... below -2.999 were defined as infra-normal." | "...1-tailed Welch's t tests... searching for lower FA and FAt values and higher FW values in the schizophrenia group."
